4.q: Trace the correct sequence linking a coast's physical landforms to the adaptation choices of its communities.
4.a: The adaptation chain runs: (1) Rocky headlands or deltaic plains set each coast's natural protection (2) Wave energy and storm-surge exposure differ between the two (3) Communities read these landform constraints (4) Kerala villages rely on natural headland shelter while low-lying Odisha builds cyclone shelters and restores mangroves. A wrong answer that prescribes sea walls for both coasts shows the student cannot connect landform type and sediment supply to suitable coastal management.

6.q: Give the correct order of zones in a coastal management plan stretching from a port headland to sandy fishing villages.
6.a: The zoning order runs: (1) Rock armour revetments guard the port headland where infrastructure value is highest (2) A mangrove regeneration belt on the intertidal mudflats attenuates waves and shields the salt pans (3) Beach nourishment with dune fencing serves the sandy village beaches (4) Setback lines keep new construction off the shifting shore. A wrong answer that applies one uniform treatment to every zone shows the student has ignored how landform and process must drive each management choice.

6.q: Give the correct order of structural units in a fold mountain belt from the Indian foreland to the Tethyan zone.
6.a: The belt crosses in order: (1) The foredeep of the foreland basin fills with young Siwalik sediments (2) The Main Boundary Thrust lifts the older Lesser Himalaya over the Sub-Himalaya (3) The Main Central Thrust stacks the high-grade Greater Himalaya above the Lesser (4) The fossil-bearing Tethyan Himalaya caps the suture side. A wrong answer that places the youngest rocks on the thrusted upper sheets shows the student has missed that compression stacks progressively older, deeper rocks over younger foreland sediments.
